displayQuote: Shall we make a new rule of life from tonight: always to try to be a little kinder than is necessary?

meta.title: Who really said "Shall we make a new rule of life from tonight: always to try to be a little kinder than is necessary?"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes — J. M. Barrie wrote it. The line appears verbatim in his 1902 novel The Little White Bird, Chapter IV. Public domain.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Shall we make a new rule of life from tonight: always to try to be a little kinder than is necessary?'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuine J. M. Barrie: the exact line is in his 1902 novel The Little White Bird, Chapter IV. Often paraphrased as 'Always be a little kinder than necessary.'

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: 1860–1937 · Scottish novelist & playwright, creator of Peter Pan
answer.sourceLine: Barrie wrote this line in his novel The Little White Bird (1902), Chapter IV, “A Night-Piece.” The wording is confirmed verbatim against the primary text; it is frequently paraphrased as “Always be a little kinder than necessary.”

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: And if not an unkindness, still might he not sometimes have been a little kinder? Shall we make a new rule of life from tonight: always to try to be a little kinder than is necessary?
trail: The exact wording is confirmed in the full text of The Little White Bird on Project Gutenberg ↗, Chapter IV.
Wikiquote ↗ lists the line in its sourced section for The Little White Bird (1902), Ch. 4, noting the common paraphrase “Always be a little kinder than necessary.”
The Little White Bird is the book in which Peter Pan first appeared, later expanded into Peter Pan in Kensington Gardens (1906) and the play Peter Pan.
source.excerptNote: The narrator watches a young husband leave the house while his wife is in labour, and turns the moment into a general resolution about kindness.

source.rightsNote: The Little White Bird was first published in 1902, well before the 1931 US public-domain cutoff, so the original text—including this line—is in the public domain in the United States.

author.metaLine: 1860–1937 · Scottish novelist & playwright, creator of Peter Pan
author.bio: Sir James Matthew Barrie (1860–1937) was a Scottish novelist and dramatist best known for creating Peter Pan. The character first appeared in The Little White Bird (1902), the same reflective, sentimental novel that contains this line about kindness. Barrie later gave the copyright in Peter Pan to Great Ormond Street Hospital for children.

misattribution.heading: The wording
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Barrie is correct, but the line is very often paraphrased, so shortened versions circulate as if they were the original.

items.who: “Always be a little kinder than necessary.”
items.why: This tidied form drops Barrie’s framing (“Shall we make a new rule of life from tonight…”) and his hedge “to try to be.” Even Wikiquote ↗ flags it as the usual paraphrase.

items.who: “always try to be a little kinder…”
items.why: Many quote sites render the middle clause as “always try to be”; Barrie’s text reads “always to try to be a little kinder than is necessary,” confirmed in the Gutenberg text ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: The thought and the words are genuinely Barrie’s, from The Little White Bird (1902), Ch. 4—just read the original passage ↗ for the full wording.

context.heading: Why it endures
lead: The line sits in a quiet, melancholy passage: Barrie’s narrator watches a young husband leave home while his wife is in labour, and wonders whether he was ever unkind to her. Out of that private moment Barrie draws a public resolution—a “new rule of life” to be kinder than strictly necessary.
The sentiment has had a long afterlife, resurfacing in graduation speeches and, more recently, in R. J. Palacio’s novel Wonder, which helped return the line to wide circulation.
